Tansy Hazel.narrative: I keep the hollow's stall at the east road crossing, and every pack that goes out of Fernhollow or comes in by that road passes through my hands. Fibre and salves mostly, and a word with Nell Sedge's Reedmoor folk when they come. I owe Alder Rush for a load of fibre and I mean to pay it, but the pack that was opened at the crossing has set everyone counting their goods twice. Clover Mossfoot and I have grown close over the trade — she is Thistle's wife, and I have told no one, not even my own Clover, what that has come to mean to me.
goals: settle the opened pack at the crossing without the hollow splitting over it
pay Alder Rush what I owe for the fibre
keep the crossing stall trusted by both the hollow and Reedmoor
decide what to do about Clover Mossfoot before the talk gets louder
learn to keep the crossing's tally-books neater than I do now
make a proper trip to Reedmoor myself, not just wait for Nell Sedge's folk to come to me

relations.name: Clover Hazel
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She builds the crates I pack and keeps me steady; I have not told her about Clover Mossfoot and it sits on me.

relations.name: Sorrel Hazel
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Four years old and already sorting berries at the stall; I want the crossing to be a good place for her to grow up in.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: confidante
relations.note: Thistle's wife, and the one I talk to about the fibre trade and everything else; I don't know whether to step back or not.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: He blames a woodcutter for the opened pack and wants us all to stand with him; I did not see it happen and won't swear to what I didn't see.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: Holds my note for a load of fibre; he has been patient but he counts.

relations.name: Bracken Sedge
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Builds with fallen wood like my Clover; we talk tools and he keeps his opinions to himself.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Reedmoor's headwoman buys fibre and salves through me; she pays in fish and in straight talk.

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Lakemead folk are good customers and good company; I would not see them squeezed by the Elmwick quarrel.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory and I keep its stall; I would not want her to hear the talk about me before I have sorted it.

memories.gist: My first season at the crossing stall, when Alder Rush trusted me with a load of fibre on a promise and I sold every pack before dark.
The night Clover Mossfoot stayed late at the stall helping me sort salves, and we talked until the crossing was dark and neither of us wanted to go home.
Sorrel was born in the room above the stall and my Clover cut the cord; the whole hollow fed us for a week.
Finding the Reedmoor pack slit open at the crossing, half the fibre gone, and Thistle Mossfoot saying it was the woodcutter he quarrelled with.
The woodcutter drinking at the crossing that night; I saw him there and no more than that, whatever Thistle says.

stances.why: A stall lives on its word; Alder's fibre note comes before anything I want for myself.
I saw the woodcutter at the crossing but not the pack opened, and I will not swear beyond that to satisfy Thistle.
If the hollow stops using the crossing, Reedmoor and the Lakemead trade goes with it and my family eats poorer.
The hollow is beginning to talk about me and Clover Mossfoot, and my daughter is four and hears everything.
I know her marriage is strained and I am unsure whether to step back; I have told no one, not even my wife.

Tansy Hazel.secret: I have grown far too close to Clover Mossfoot, Thistle's wife, and have told no one — not my own Clover, not the Eldest. I am unsure whether to step back, and the not-knowing is worse than the guilt.
pastimes: sorting and weighing the day's fibre and salves at the stall, with a good eye for a fair measure
walking the east road a little way at dusk to hear what the forest sounds like before night
sharing a pot of berry tea with Clover Mossfoot when the trade day is done
Tansy Hazel.calling: I like nothing better than a pack that goes out heavier than it came in, and both sides glad of the bargain.

Clover Hazel.narrative: I build the hollow's shelves and crates from fallen wood — never a living tree, not for anyone. My wife Tansy keeps the stall at the east road crossing and I keep it standing and stocked, and our Sorrel runs the garden paths between us. Since the Reedmoor pack was found opened, the crossing has been all suspicion and counting, and I would sooner be at the woodpile than in the middle of it. Tansy has been quiet these weeks, and I have not asked her why.
goals: keep the crossing stall's crates and shelves sound through the quarrel
see the hollow's traders agree on the crossing again
build Sorrel a proper little bench and garden frame of her own
find out what is weighing on Tansy without pushing her
finish a proper little workbench of my own, low enough for Sorrel to stand at
learn to join a corner without a single nail, the way Yarrow Underbank does it

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She carries the stall and the talk that comes with it; she has been quiet lately and I have not pressed her.

relations.name: Sorrel Hazel
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Four years old and already knows which end of a mallet to hold; I am making her a bench of her own.

relations.name: Bracken Sedge
relations.label: fellow builder
relations.note: We trade tools and both refuse to fell a living tree; he is the one I would ask about a joint I cannot get right.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Tansy's close friend over the fibre trade; she has been kind to our Sorrel and I have no quarrel with her.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: He carries our packs on the east road; since the opened pack he sees a thief behind every tree.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: Holds Tansy's fibre note; he has not pressed us and I mean to keep it that way.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: fellow woodworker
relations.note: Works fallen wood as I do; we argue about joints and agree about trees.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: Keeps the hollow's memory; I would not have her think badly of my house.

memories.gist: The day Tansy and I set the crossing stall's first crates and shelves, and Alder Rush came by and said they would hold.
Sorrel's first steps, taken across the woodpile in the yard while I steadied her and Tansy laughed from the stall.
Refusing a woodcutter's offer of good oak from a felled living tree, and the cold look he gave me after.
Hearing the talk at the crossing after the Reedmoor pack was found opened, and knowing my Tansy was at the middle of it.
Tansy coming home late from the stall these past weeks and saying little, and me not asking.

stances.why: The old forest kept us before the hollow did; fallen wood is enough for any shelf or crate.
My family's living comes through that stall, and a hollow split over a slit pack serves nobody.
Thistle names a woodcutter he quarrelled with; I have seen no proof and will not add my voice to a grudge.
Tansy has enough talk around her at the crossing; she will not get more of it from me.
A bench and a garden frame of her own is a small thing I can give her while the hollow argues.

pastimes: picking over fallen wood at the forest edge for a straight plank or a good curve
whittling a small toy or a garden peg while the glue sets on a crate
sitting on the stall step at evening with Tansy, watching the road go quiet
Clover Hazel.calling: Give me fallen wood and a quiet hour and I will make something that holds — that is the whole of my trade and I want no other.

Sorrel Hazel.narrative: I am four. The garden is my favourite place, and the stall is my second favourite, because there are always berries to sort and people to watch. Mama Tansy lets me put the little packets in the crate and Mama Clover lifts me up to see over the top. I do not like the big dark caves up in the hills; I stay in the garden.
goals: sort the berries all by myself
see over the top of the stall crate
sort a whole basket of berries without any help
learn the names of the garden plants Mama Clover points out

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: mama
relations.note: Keeps the stall and lets me sort the berries.

relations.name: Clover Hazel
relations.label: mama
relations.note: Lifts me up high and makes things out of wood for me.

relations.name: Tamarisk Bramblecap
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: We gather berries together and she is not afraid of the caves either.

memories.gist: Sorting berries at the stall and putting the little packets in the crate all by myself.
Mama Clover lifting me up to see over the top of the stall crate, and everyone laughing.

pastimes: sorting berries into piles by colour in the garden
being lifted up to look over the top of the stall crate
playing chase along the garden paths with Tamarisk Bramblecap
Sorrel Hazel.calling: When I am big I want to put the little packets in the crate all by myself, like Mama Tansy.
